faq.q: Which rebar bender do I need for 15M, 20M and 25M bars?
faq.a: A B 36 or BS 36 bends single bars up to 35M (#11) and two 20M bars at once in normal steel, and is the usual choice for a rebar shop running 10M to 25M. For site work on 10M–20M a portable BT 26 or MG 26 Junior on 110/220 V is enough. For 30M–45M bars choose a B 45x1, B 50 or the BS 50/BS 60.

faq.q: Can I run a rebar bender on single-phase power?
faq.a: Yes — the portable MG 20B, MG 26 Junior, BT 24x5 and BT 26 benders and the POWER 24 cutter have a built-in transformer and run on 110 V or 220 V single-phase. The stationary B, BS, SL, SX, H, M and SH machines are three-phase and are supplied for 600 V; 208 V, 240 V or 480 V are available on request.

faq.q: Do the machines come with a CSA-approved electrical panel?
faq.a: Yes. Every machine NovoTech supplies has a CSA-approved electrical panel wired for Canadian voltage, with overload protection on the benders.

faq.q: Can a standard rebar bender make stirrups?
faq.a: Yes. The B series and the portable BT benders make stirrups with the standard pins and rollers; an optional spiral stirrup attachment is available for B and BS series only. For continuous stirrup production from coil use the automatic SLS 12 on the automatic lines page.

faq.q: What does the 45 / 65 / 85 kg/mm² capacity mean?
faq.a: The three columns are the manufacturer's ratings for rebar of different tensile strengths: 45 kg/mm² (≈ 64,000 psi), 65 kg/mm² (≈ 92,500 psi) and 85 kg/mm² (≈ 120,900 psi). Canadian Grade 400W rebar has a minimum tensile strength of 540 MPa (≈ 55 kg/mm²), so the 65 kg/mm² column is a safe guide for everyday Canadian bar.

faq.q: Are spare parts, blades and tooling available in Canada?
faq.a: Yes. NovoTech stocks cutting blades, bending pins, rollers and electrical parts for GMS machines in Mississauga, Ontario, and provides technical support, installation and training.
